Thanks for the update. With full clearance to return to baseline and reintroduce posterior work, we’ll roll everything back into a cohesive 12-week plan. This version preserves the prior emphasis on posterior chain development, the two conditioning sessions per week, and the structured progression, while integrating the rehab history and the current clearance. I’ll present a clear week-by-week, day-by-day plan with sets, reps, and progression notes, plus basic guidance on loads and RPE.

Assumptions and structure
- Training days: 4 resistance days per week (Upper A, Upper B, Lower/Posterior-lite, Lower/Posterior-focused once per week), plus 2 conditioning days (Conditioning A and Conditioning B) and 1–2 optional mobility days as needed.
- Phase layout:
  - Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundation, technique, posterior base, light mastery of hinge patterns, introduction of conditioning.
  - Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Hypertrophy base with strong posterior emphasis, mid-range loading on main lifts, higher posterior volume.
  - Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Strength concentration and peak, heavy main lifts with targeted posterior chain strength, refine technique and carryover.
- Conditioning: 2 weekly sessions (A and B) of 20–25 minutes each, non-fatiguing to support recovery and aerobic base.
- Nutrition and recovery: continue baseline benchmarks (protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day, 7–9 hours sleep, hydration, general micronutrient needs). Adjust calories to support strength and body composition goals.

Phase 1: Foundation & Technique (Weeks 1–4)
Goals: technique mastery, establish a robust strength base, build conditioning tolerance, and reinforce posterior-chain awareness.

Week 1
- Day 1: Lower 1 – Squat emphasis + posterior accessory
  - Back squat: 3 x 5 at 70% 1RM (tempo 2-0-1)
  - Front squat: 3 x 6 at 60–65%
  - Romanian deadlift (RDL): 3 x 8 (light–moderate)
  - Hip thrust or glute bridge (moderate emphasis): 3 x 8
  - Walking or farmer’s carry: 2 x 40–60 seconds
  - Core: planks 3 x 30–45 seconds
- Day 2: Upper A – Horizontal push/pull
  - Bench press: 3 x 5 at 70%
  - Dumbbell floor press or close-grip bench: 3 x 8
  - Seated cable row: 3 x 10
  - Lat pulldown: 3 x 8–10
  - Face pulls: 3 x 12
  - Biceps curls: 3 x 12
  - Triceps pushdown: 3 x 12
- Day 3: Rest / Mobility
- Day 4: Upper B – Vertical push/pull
  - Overhead press (DB or barbell): 3 x 6
  - Arnold press or landmine press: 3 x 8
  - Chest-supported row or A1 row: 3 x 8
  - Lat pulldown: 3 x 8–10
  - Lateral raises: 3 x 12
  - Pallof presses: 3 x 30–40 seconds
- Day 5: Lower 2 – Hinge emphasis
  - Hip thrust: 4 x 8
  - Romanian deadlift: 3 x 8
  - Leg curl: 3 x 12
  - Split squats or bulgarian split squats: 3 x 8 per leg
  - Ab work: 3 x 12–15
- Day 6: Conditioning A
  - 20–25 min steady-state cardio (bike, row, or elliptical) at RPE 5–6
- Day 7: Rest / Mobility

Week 2
- Increase main lifts by small increments if technique is solid; target RPE 7–8 on main lifts.
- Squat: 3 x 5 at 72–75%
- Front squat: 3 x 6 at 62–67%
- Bench: 3 x 5 at 72–75%
- OHP: 3 x 6 at 62–67%
- Deadlift: 3 x 5 at 67–70% (light, technique-focused)
- RDL: 3 x 8 at 60–65%
- Accessory volume similar to Week 1; add one set to a hinge or posterior accessory if tolerated
- Core: 3 x 30–45 seconds

Week 3
- Progress main lifts: Squat 3 x 5 at 75–77%; Bench 3 x 5 at 78–80%; OHP 3 x 6 at 65–70%
- Deadlift 3 x 5 at 70–72% (progressively heavier within form)
- RDL 3 x 8 at 62–67%
- Posterior accessories: Hip thrust 4 x 8; Back extension 3 x 12
- Core: 3 x 30–60 seconds
- Conditioning A: 20–25 min moderate

Week 4 (Deload / Technique check)
- Lower volume; main lifts at 60–70% for 2–3 sets of 6–8
- Accessory movements reduced; emphasize technique and bracing
- Conditioning A: 15–20 min light cardio
- Rehab/rehab-like mobility work if needed for any niggles

Phase 2: Hypertrophy Base with Posterior Emphasis (Weeks 5–8)
Goals: hypertrophy-focused training with increased posterior-chain volume; maintain deadlift readiness and technique with safe loading.

Week 5
- Day 1: Lower 1 – Squat emphasis + posterior accessories
  - Back squat: 4 x 6 at 70–75%
  - Front squat: 3 x 8
  - Hip thrust: 4 x 8
  - RDL: 3 x 8
  - Hamstring curl: 3 x 12
  - Core: 3 x 12–15
- Day 2: Upper A
  - Bench: 4 x 6
  - Incline DB: 3 x 8–10
  - Seated row: 3 x 8–10
  - Lat pulldown: 3 x 8–10
  - Face pulls: 3 x 12–15
  - Curls: 3 x 12
- Day 3: Rest / Mobility
- Day 4: Lower 2 – Posterior emphasis
  - Deadlift (heavy variation delayed; use light to moderate as a pattern only if cleared by clinician; otherwise substitute with trap-bar deadlift or rack pulls from knee height): 3 x 5 at 60–70% or 3 x 5 at a light to moderate load
  - Barbell row: 3 x 8
  - Glute-ham raise progressions: 3 x 6–8
  - Leg press or split squats: 3 x 10
  - Core: 3 x 12–15
- Day 5: Upper B
  - OHP: 4 x 6
  - Lateral raises: 3 x 12
  - Chest-supported row: 3 x 8
  - Lat pulldown: 3 x 8–10
  - Pallof presses: 3 x 30–40s
- Day 6: Conditioning A
  - 20–25 min steady cardio
- Day 7: Conditioning B
  - 20–25 min intervals (short intervals if tolerated, but keep RPE 6–7)

Week 6
- Increase overall posterior volume and intensity cautiously
- Back squats and bench: similar structure with small load increases if technique remains solid
- Deadlift pattern: if available and cleared, progress to light trap-bar or rack pulls to maintain posterior chain engagement
- Posterior work: hip thrusts, RDLs, glute ham raises or progressions
- Conditioning: 20 minutes, low to moderate intensity

Week 7
- Week 7 introduces slightly heavier hinge exposure if tolerating
- Day 1: Lower 1
  - Back squat: 4 x 6–8 at 72–77%
  - Front squat: 3 x 8
  - Hip thrust: 4 x 8
  - RDL: 3 x 8 or 3 x 6 depending on tolerance
- Day 2: Upper A
  - Bench: 4 x 6–8
  - Incline DB: 3 x 8–10
  - Seated row: 3 x 8–10
  - Lat pulldown: 3 x 8–10
  - Face pulls: 3 x 12–15
- Day 3: Rest / Mobility
- Day 4: Lower 2
  - Rack pulls or light conventional deadlift (if cleared) from knee height: 3 x 5 at light weight
  - Barbell row: 3 x 8
  - Leg press: 3 x 10
  - Core: 3 x 12–15
- Day 5: Upper B
  - OHP: 4 x 6–8
  - Lateral raises: 3 x 12
  - Cable reverse flyes: 3 x 12
  - Shrugs: 3 x 12
- Day 6: Conditioning A
  - 20–25 min moderate cardio
- Day 7: Conditioning B
  - 20–25 min intervals or steady state depending on recovery

Week 8
- Slight deload / technique emphasis week
- Maintain posterior focus but reduce overall work volume
- Main lifts at 60–70% for 2–3 sets of 6–8
- Accessory posterior work: 2–3 exercises per session with good form
- Conditioning: 15–20 minutes light cardio

Phase 3: Strength Concentration & Peak (Weeks 9–12)
Goals: peak strength on primary lifts with robust posterior chain support, maintain hypertrophy, and refine technique with controlled volumes.

Week 9
- Day 1: Lower 1 – Squat emphasis + posterior accessories
  - Back squat: 5 x 5 at 80–85%
  - Front squat: 3 x 6 at 70–75%
  - Hip thrust: 4 x 6
  - RDL: 3 x 6
  - Core: 3 x 40–60 seconds
- Day 2: Upper A
  - Bench press: 5 x 5 at 82–85%
  - Incline DB: 3 x 8
  - Seated row: 3 x 8–10
  - Lat pulldown: 3 x 8–10
  - Face pulls: 3 x 12
  - Curls: 3 x 12
- Day 3: Rest / Mobility
- Day 4: Lower 2 – Posterior emphasis
  - Deadlift pattern alternative (heavy to lighten as needed): 5 x 3 at 85–90% if cleared and pain-free; otherwise trap-bar deadlift 3 x 5 from mid-throke
  - Barbell row: 4 x 6
  - Glute-ham raises or reverse hypers: 3 x 8
  - Leg curls: 3 x 12
  - Core: 3 x 12–15
- Day 5: Upper B
  - OHP: 5 x 5 at 82–85%
  - Lateral raises: 3 x 12
  - Chest-supported row: 3 x 8
  - Lat pulldown: 3 x 8–10
  - Pallof presses: 3 x 40s
- Day 6: Conditioning A
  - 20–25 min moderate cardio
- Day 7: Conditioning B
  - 20–25 min intervals or light cardio as tolerated

Week 10
- Week 10: heavy but controlled
- Day 1: Squat 5 x 4 at 85–90%
- Day 2: Bench 5 x 4 at 85%
- Day 3: Rest / Mobility
- Day 4: Deadlift 5 x 3 at 85–90% (if cleared and pain-free)
- Day 5: Overhead press 4 x 5 at 75–80%
- Day 6: Accessory and core
- Day 7: Conditioning A or rest

Week 11
- Week 11: peaking in main lifts
- Day 1: Squat 4 x 4 at 88–92%
- Day 2: Bench 4 x 4 at 88–92%
- Day 3: Rest / Mobility
- Day 4: Deadlift 4 x 2–3 at 90–95% (top single if appropriate)
- Day 5: OHP 3 x 5 at 78–82%
- Day 6: Rows / pulls 3–4 x 6–8
- Day 7: Conditioning A or rest

Week 12: Testing/Performance Week
- Option: formal 1RM testing or competitive-style lifting blocks
- Squat: 2–3 x 2–3 at 92–96% or 1RM test
- Bench: 2–3 x 2–3 at 92–96% or 1RM test
- Deadlift: 2–3 x 2–3 at 92–96% or 1RM test
- OHP: 3 x 3 at 85–88%
- Accessory: minimal; focus on posterior maintenance and mobility if not testing

Notes on progression and loads
- Use RPE targets to gauge progression:
  - Weeks 1–4: main lifts RPE 7–8
  - Weeks 5–8: main lifts stay in hypertrophy range, RPE ~7–8
  - Weeks 9–12: main lifts at RPE 8–9 for strength, but take care to avoid form breakdown
- Incremental loading: standard 2.5–5 lb increments for upper body; 5–10 lb increments for lower body when form and RPE permit
- Deloads: include an active deload during Week 4 and Week 8; adjust if fatigue accumulates
- Posterior chain emphasis: maintain 2–3 dedicated posterior work sessions per week (glute bridges, hip thrusts, RDLs, back extensions, rows, face pulls), progressively increasing volume in Weeks 5–12
- Conditioning: 2 sessions per week; keep at 20–25 minutes; ensure no undue fatigue on heavy lifting days

Safety and injury considerations
- Warm-ups: include 5–10 minutes general warm-up plus 5–10 minutes movement prep targeted to the day’s main lifts
- Form: emphasize bracing, neutral spine, and controlled tempo
- Recovery: ensure sleep, nutrition, hydration are aligned with the increased training load; consider a 1–2 day deload if fatigue signs persist
- Adjustments: if any pain or discomfort arises (new or recurring), adjust volume/loads or substitute with safer variations, and consult with the client’s clinician if needed

Optional add-ons
- Mobility and activation work on off days: hip flexor/quad mobility, thoracic spine mobility, and scapular stabilization to support posture during heavy pulls
- Technique-only days: light technique days to reinforce form on main lifts with ample rest
